events.label: Sherlock Holmes speaks about life and fiction

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: life is infinitely stranger than anything which the mind of man could invent; we would not dare to conceive the things which are really mere commonplaces of existence; if we could fly out of that window hand in hand, hover over this great city, gently remove the roofs, and peep in at the queer things which are going on, the strange coincidences, the plannings, the cross-purposes, the wonderful chains of events, working through generations, and leading to the most outré results, it would make all fiction with its conventionalities and foreseen conclusions most stale and unprofitable.

events.label: The speaker answers that he is not convinced

communicates.speaker: unknown
communicates.content: And yet I am not convinced of it.

events.label: The speaker states that cases in papers are bald and vulgar

communicates.speaker: unknown
communicates.content: The cases which come to light in the papers are, as a rule, bald enough, and vulgar enough; we have in our police reports realism pushed to its extreme limits, and yet the result is, it must be confessed, neither fascinating nor artistic.

events.label: Sherlock Holmes remarks that realistic effect requires selection and discretion

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: A certain selection and discretion must be used in producing a realistic effect.

events.label: Sherlock Holmes remarks that the police report lacks details and stresses platitudes

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: This is wanting in the police report, where more stress is laid, perhaps, upon the platitudes of the magistrate than upon the details, which to an observer contain the vital essence of the whole matter.

events.label: Sherlock Holmes says the commonplace is unnatural

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Depend upon it, there is nothing so unnatural as the commonplace.

events.label: The speaker smiles and shakes his head
The speaker says he can understand Holmes's thinking

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I can quite understand your thinking so.

events.label: The speaker says Holmes is brought into contact with strange and bizarre things

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Of course, in your position of unofficial adviser and helper to everybody who is absolutely puzzled, throughout three continents, you are brought in contact with all that is strange and bizarre.

events.label: The speaker picks up the morning paper from the ground and presents it for a practical test
The speaker identifies the newspaper heading about a husband's cruelty to his wife

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Here is the first heading upon which I come. 'A husband's cruelty to his wife.' There is half a column of print, but I know without reading it that it is all perfectly familiar to me.

events.label: Holmes says the Dundas separation case is an unfortunate example for the argument

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Indeed, your example is an unfortunate one for your argument.

events.label: Holmes identifies the case as the Dundas separation case and says he had been clearing up some small points in connection with it

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: This is the Dundas separation case, and, as it happens, I was engaged in clearing up some small points in connection with it.

events.label: Holmes describes the husband, wife, and conduct complained of in the Dundas separation case

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The husband was a teetotaler, there was no other woman, and the conduct complained of was that he had drifted into the habit of winding up every meal by taking out his false teeth and hurling them at his wife, which, you will allow, is not an action likely to occur to the imagination of the average story-teller.

events.label: Holmes offers snuff to the doctor and tells him to acknowledge Holmes has scored over him

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Take a pinch of snuff, Doctor, and acknowledge that I have scored over you in your example.

events.label: Holmes mentions a souvenir from the King of Bohemia

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It is a little souvenir from the King of Bohemia in return for my assistance in the case of the Irene Adler papers.

events.label: Holmes mentions a ring from the reigning family of Holland

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It was from the reigning family of Holland, though the matter in which I served them was of such delicacy that I cannot confide it even to you, who have been good enough to chronicle one or two of my little problems.

events.label: Holmes states that he has several matters on hand

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Some ten or twelve, but none which present any feature of interest. They are important, you understand, without being interesting. Indeed, I have found that it is usually in unimportant matters that there is a field for the observation, and for the quick analysis of cause and effect which gives the charm to an investigation. The larger crimes are apt to be the simpler, for the bigger the crime the more obvious, as a rule, is the motive. In these cases, save for one rather intricate matter which has been referred to me from Marseilles, there is nothing which presents any features of interest. It is possible, however, that I may have something better before very many minutes are over, for this is one of my clients, or I am much mistaken.

events.label: Holmes rises and stands by the window
The large woman stands on the pavement opposite and then hurries across the road to the bell
Holmes remarks on the woman's short sight and typewriting

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Do you not find that with your short sight it is a little trying to do so much typewriting?

events.label: The woman replies that she now types without looking at the letters

communicates.speaker: large_woman
communicates.content: I did at first, but now I know where the letters are without looking.

events.label: The woman reacts with fear and astonishment
The woman asks Holmes how he knew about her

communicates.speaker: large_woman
communicates.content: You’ve heard about me, Mr. Holmes, else how could you know all that?

events.label: Holmes laughs and replies that knowing things is his business

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Never mind. It is my business to know things. Perhaps I have trained myself to see what others overlook. If not, why should you come to consult me?

events.label: The woman explains why she came to Holmes and asks him to help find Hosmer Angel

communicates.speaker: large_woman
communicates.content: I came to you, sir, because I heard of you from Mrs. Etherege, whose husband you found so easy when the police and everyone had given him up for dead. Oh, Mr. Holmes, I wish you would do as much for me. I’m not rich, but still I have a hundred a year in my own right, besides the little that I make by the machine, and I would give it all to know what has become of Mr. Hosmer Angel.

events.label: Holmes asks why she came away to consult him in such a hurry

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Why did you come away to consult me in such a hurry?

events.label: Mary Sutherland says she bangs out of the house and comes right away to Holmes

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Yes, I did bang out of the house, for it made me angry to see the easy way in which Mr. Windibank—that is, my father—took it all. He would not go to the police, and he would not go to you, and so at last, as he would do nothing and kept on saying that there was no harm done, it made me mad, and I just on with my things and came right away to you.

events.label: Holmes remarks that Windibank is Mary Sutherland's stepfather

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Your father, your stepfather, surely, since the name is different.

events.label: Mary Sutherland says Windibank is her stepfather and that she calls him father

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Yes, my stepfather. I call him father, though it sounds funny, too, for he is only five years and two months older than myself.

events.label: Holmes asks whether Mary Sutherland's mother is alive

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And your mother is alive?

events.label: Mary Sutherland says her mother is alive and well

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Oh, yes, mother is alive and well.

events.label: Mary Sutherland says her mother remarried soon after her father's death

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: I wasn’t best pleased, Mr. Holmes, when she married again so soon after father’s death, and a man who was nearly fifteen years younger than herself.

events.label: Mary Sutherland describes her father, mother, Mr. Hardy, and Mr. Windibank's role in the business

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Father was a plumber in the Tottenham Court Road, and he left a tidy business behind him, which mother carried on with Mr. Hardy, the foreman; but when Mr. Windibank came he made her sell the business, for he was very superior, being a traveller in wines. They got £4700 for the goodwill and interest, which wasn’t near as much as father could have got if he had been alive.

events.label: Holmes listens to Mary Sutherland's narrative with concentration
Mary Sutherland says her income is separate from the business and was left to her by her uncle

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Oh, no, sir. It is quite separate and was left me by my uncle Ned in Auckland. It is in New Zealand stock, paying 41/2 per cent. Two thousand five hundred pounds was the amount, but I can only touch the interest.

events.label: Holmes remarks that Mary Sutherland interests him extremely

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You interest me extremely.

events.label: Holmes comments on Mary Sutherland's income and travel habits

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And since you draw so large a sum as a hundred a year, with what you earn into the bargain, you no doubt travel a little and indulge yourself in every way. I believe that a single lady can get on very nicely upon an income of about £60.

events.label: Mary Sutherland says she could live on less and does not wish to be a burden while staying at home

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: I could do with much less than that, Mr. Holmes, but you understand that as long as I live at home I don’t wish to be a burden to them, and so they have the use of the money just while I am staying with them. Of course, that is only just for the time.

events.label: Mr. Windibank pays interest to mother Sutherland every quarter
Miss Sutherland earns money by typewriting and produces sheets in a day
Holmes speaks to Miss Sutherland and Watson and asks about Hosmer Angel

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You have made your position very clear to me. This is my friend, Dr. Watson, be- fore whom you can speak as freely as before myself. Kindly tell us now all about your connection with Mr. Hosmer Angel.

events.label: Miss Sutherland flushes and picks nervously at her jacket fringe
Miss Sutherland describes first meeting Hosmer Angel at the gasfitters' ball

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: I met him first at the gasfitters’ ball.

events.label: Miss Sutherland describes receiving ball tickets from father and mother after his death

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: They used to send father tickets when he was alive, and then afterwards they remembered us, and sent them to mother.

events.label: Mr. Windibank objects to Miss Sutherland going out

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Mr. Windibank did not wish us to go. He never did wish us to go anywhere.

events.label: Mr. Windibank becomes angry when Miss Sutherland wants to join a Sunday-school treat

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: He would get quite mad if I wanted so much as to join a Sunday-school treat.

events.label: Miss Sutherland insists on going to the ball despite Mr. Windibank's objections

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: But this time I was set on going, and I would go; for what right had he to prevent?

events.label: Mr. Windibank says the guests are not fit for Miss Sutherland and her family to know

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: He said the folk were not fit for us to know, when all father’s friends were to be there.

events.label: Mr. Windibank says Miss Sutherland has nothing fit to wear

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: And he said that I had nothing fit to wear, when I had my purple plush that I had never so much as taken out of the drawer.

events.label: He goes to France on the firm's business, and Mary Sutherland goes with Mr. Hardy and her mother
Mary Sutherland meets Hosmer Angel at the gasfitters' ball
Windibank returns from France and reacts to Mary Sutherland's going to the ball
Holmes states that Windibank may have been annoyed when he returned from France

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I suppose that when Mr. Windibank came back from France he was very annoyed at your having gone to the ball.

events.label: Holmes identifies the gasfitters' ball as the place where Mary Sutherland met Hosmer Angel

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Then at the gasfitters' ball you met, as I understand, a gentleman called Mr. Hosmer Angel.

events.label: Mary Sutherland meets Hosmer Angel, receives a visit the next day, meets him twice for walks, and then he can no longer come to the house after her father returns

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: I met him that night, and he called next day to ask if we had got home all safe, and after that we met him twice for walks, but after that father came back again, and Mr. Hosmer Angel could not come to the house any more.

events.label: Mary Sutherland explains that her father disliked visitors and expected women to stay within their family circle

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Well, you know father didn’t like anything of the sort. He wouldn’t have any visitors if he could help it, and he used to say that a woman should be happy in her own family circle. But then, as I used to say to mother, a woman wants her own circle to begin with, and I had not got mine yet.

events.label: Mary Sutherland says Hosmer Angel did not see her before Father left for France

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Well, father was going off to France again in a week, and Hosmer wrote and said that it would be safer and better not to see each other until he had gone. We could write in the meantime, and he used to write every day. I took the letters in in the morning, so there was no need for father to know. Oh, yes, Mr. Holmes.

events.label: The couple become engaged after their first walk
Hosmer Angel works as a cashier in an office in Leadenhall Street
Hosmer Angel sleeps on the premises in Leadenhall Street
Mary Sutherland addresses her letters to the Leadenhall Street Post Office to be left till called for
Hosmer Angel says letters sent to the office would cause him to be chaffed by the other clerks

communicates.speaker: hosmer_angel
communicates.content: if they were sent to the office he would be chaffed by all the other clerks about having letters from a lady

events.label: Mary Sutherland offers to typewrite her letters like Hosmer Angel did his
Hosmer Angel refuses the typewritten letters
Hosmer Angel says typewritten letters would make the machine come between them

communicates.speaker: hosmer_angel
communicates.content: when I wrote them they seemed to come from me, but when they were typewritten he always felt that the machine had come between us

events.label: Holmes says the little things are important

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It was most suggestive. It has long been an axiom of mine that the little things are infinitely the most important.

events.label: Holmes asks Mary Sutherland about other little things concerning Hosmer Angel

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Can you remember any other little things about Mr. Hosmer Angel?

events.label: Mary Sutherland describes Hosmer Angel as shy and retiring

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: He was a very shy man, Mr. Holmes. He would rather walk with me in the evening than in the daylight, for he said that he hated to be conspicuous. Very retiring and gentlemanly he was. Even his voice was gentle. He’d had the quinsy and swollen glands when he was young, he told me, and it had left him with a weak throat, and a hesitating, whispering fashion of speech. He was always well dressed, very neat and plain, but his eyes were weak, just as mine are, and he wore tinted glasses against the glare.

events.label: Holmes asks what happened when Windibank returned to France

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Well, and what happened when Mr. Windibank, your stepfather, returned to France?

events.label: Mary Sutherland says Hosmer Angel returned and proposed marriage

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Mr. Hosmer Angel came to the house again and proposed that we should marry before father came back.

events.label: The man makes the woman swear loyalty on the Testament

communicates.speaker: hosmer_angel
communicates.content: whatever happened I would always be true to him

events.label: Mother approves the oath and describes it as a sign of passion

communicates.speaker: mother_sutherland
communicates.content: he was quite right to make me swear, and that it was a sign of his passion

events.label: Mother favors the man more than Mary does
They discuss marrying within the week and instruct Mary to tell father afterward

communicates.speaker: mother_sutherland
communicates.content: never to mind about father, but just to tell him afterwards

events.label: Mary asks about father and writes to him at Bordeaux
Father's letter returns undelivered on the morning of the wedding
Father starts to England before the letter arrives
Holmes asks whether the wedding was arranged for Friday and whether it was to be in church

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: that was unfortunate. Your wedding was arranged, then, for the Friday. Was it to be in church?

events.label: Mary confirms the wedding was to be very quiet and in church

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Yes, sir, but very quietly. It was to be at St.

events.label: Hosmer Angel arrives in a hansom and takes the four-wheeler
The two passengers ride in the hansom while Hosmer Angel rides in the four-wheeler
Watson and Mary Sutherland arrive at the church before the four-wheeler
The cabman finds that no one is in the four-wheeler
The cabman says he cannot imagine what became of Hosmer Angel and says he saw him get in

communicates.speaker: cabman
communicates.content: he could not imagine what had become of him, for he had seen him get in with his own eyes

events.label: Watson says that he has had no further indication of Hosmer Angel since last Friday

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: That was last Friday, Mr. Holmes, and I have never seen or heard anything since then to throw any light upon what became of him

events.label: Holmes says Watson has been shamefully treated

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It seems to me that you have been very shamefully treated

events.label: Mary Sutherland says Hosmer was too good and kind to leave her and recalls his wedding-morning warning.

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Oh, no, sir! He was too good and kind to leave me so. Why, all the morning he was saying to me that, whatever happened, I was to be true; and that even if something quite unforeseen occurred to separate us, I was always to remember that I was pledged to him, and that he would claim his pledge sooner or later. It seemed strange talk for a wedding-morning, but what has happened since gives a meaning to it.

events.label: Holmes asks whether Mary thinks an unforeseen catastrophe occurred to Hosmer.

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Your own opinion is, then, that some unforeseen catastrophe has occurred to him?

events.label: Mary says she believes Hosmer foresaw danger and that what he foresaw happened.

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Yes, sir. I believe that he foresaw some danger, or else he would not have talked so. And then I think that what he foresaw happened.

events.label: Holmes asks what happened to Hosmer and whether Mary has any notion of it.

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: But you have no notion as to what it could have been?

events.label: Holmes asks how Mary’s mother reacted and Mary says her mother became angry and forbade further discussion.

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: One more question. How did your mother take the matter?

events.label: Holmes asks whether Mary told her father and Mary says he seemed to think something had happened and that she should hear of Hosmer again.

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And your father? Did you tell him?

events.label: Mary sobs into her handkerchief.
Holmes says he will examine the case and asks for the matter to be left to him

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I shall glance into the case for you, and I have no doubt that we shall reach some definite result. Let the weight of the matter rest upon me now, and do not let your mind dwell upon it further.

events.label: Holmes tells Mary Sutherland to let Mr. Hosmer Angel vanish from her memory

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Above all, try to let Mr. Hosmer Angel vanish from your memory, as he has done from your life.

events.label: Mary Sutherland asks whether she will see Hosmer Angel again

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Then you don’t think I’ll see him again?

events.label: Mary Sutherland asks what has happened to Hosmer Angel

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Then what has happened to him?

events.label: Holmes says he will handle the question and asks for a description and letters

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You will leave that question in my hands. I should like an accurate description of him and any letters of his which you can spare.

events.label: Mary Sutherland says she advertised for Hosmer Angel in the Chronicle

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: I advertised for him in last Saturday’s Chronicle.

events.label: Mary Sutherland gives Holmes the newspaper slip and four letters

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: Here is the slip and here are four letters from him.

events.label: Holmes asks Mary Sutherland for her address

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And your address?

events.label: Mary Sutherland gives her address as 31 Lyon Place, Camberwell

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: 31 Lyon Place, Camberwell.

events.label: Holmes says he understands that Mary Sutherland never had Mr. Angel's address and asks about her father's business

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Mr. Angel’s address you never had, I understand. Where is your father’s place of business?

events.label: Mary Sutherland states that her father travels for Westhouse & Marbank of Fenchurch Street

communicates.speaker: mary_sutherland
communicates.content: He travels for Westhouse & Marbank, the great claret importers of Fenchurch Street.

events.label: Holmes thanks Mary Sutherland and tells her to leave the papers and keep the incident secret

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Thank you. You have made your statement very clearly. You will leave the papers here, and remember the advice which I have given you. Let the whole incident be a sealed book, and do not allow it to affect your life.

events.label: Holmes explains his reasoning about Hosmer Angel, the stepfather, and the disguise

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It was obvious from the first that this Mr. Hosmer Angel must have some strong object for his curious conduct, and it was equally clear that the only man who really profited by the incident, as far as we could see, was the stepfather. Then the fact that the two men were never together, but that the one always appeared when the other was away, was suggestive. So were the tinted spectacles and the curious voice, which both hinted at a disguise, as did the bushy whiskers.

clues.significance: Holmes inferred that Mary Sutherland had advertised for Hosmer Angel from the newspaper slip she produced.
Holmes inferred that the woman's sleeve material could show traces from her activities
Holmes inferred that the wrist mark matched a typewritist's pressure against a table
Holmes inferred short sight and typewriting from the pince-nez marks at either side of her nose
Holmes inferred that the signature was likely used to make denial possible because it was typewritten.
Holmes inferred that the four letters shared the same typewriter characteristics, including slurred 'e's, tailless 'r's, and fourteen other matching marks.
Holmes inferred a disguise from the tinted spectacles.
Holmes inferred a disguise from the bushy whiskers.
The typewriter's peculiarities served as evidence for identifying the man.
